retraction_records.what: RETRACTION - the earlier claim that the code-graph calls view under-reports cross-crate call sites is FALSE and must not reach curation. The trace shows q4 calls and q5 refs each returned 41 rows for from_toml_str, db_state=fresh, across 6 files in 5 crates; the rows=1 belonged to q3 (pid_format). The 1 was produced by piping q4 output through head -30, which cut 41 records to 10, leaving conductor-cli/paths.rs as the only visible non-test caller - then attributing that to the graph. The same habit corrupted the PId finding: q1 carried a self-imposed LIMIT 40 and returned exactly 40, which was read as the complete set and written up as no references outside the test module; the true count is 82 refs across 16 files in 6 crates. grep did not beat the graph - grep over-counts (pub fn definition, 4 test-function names, 1 doc comment). The real friction is an orchestrator reading a self-truncated view as a result set and blaming the tool. Operator caught it before apply. Artifacts corrected: research.md Graph impact (with an inline correction note), plan.md Implementation notes and Provenance; the generalized grep-before-trusting-the-graph directive was removed and replaced with the narrow true lesson (SCIP matches by descriptor; attribute a row count to its query; never read a LIMIT-ed or head-ed view as the result; graph lines are 0-indexed vs grep 1-indexed).
